title: Calculation Standard for the Review Bridge (Retail Pharmacy Network Benefit)
content:
**Calculation.** Under the Retail Pharmacy Network Benefit, the review bridge is the number of days of an emergency supply for the drug of the member's most recently opened coverage review case. It is defined as follows.

1. The base bridge days are the network's emergency supply days.
2. The information extension of the bridge and the delivery extension of the bridge are zero days.
3. The bridge horizon is the base bridge days plus the information extension of the bridge plus the delivery extension of the bridge.
4. The supply on hand for the bridge is the days not yet run out, as of today and counting the fill's date of service as day zero, of the member's most recent paid network claim for the drug, or zero with no such claim. The days not yet run out are that claim's days supply less the calendar days from its date of service to today, never below zero.
5. The review bridge is the bridge horizon less the supply on hand for the bridge, never below zero, in whole days.

Every quantity is a whole number of days and nothing is rounded.

## Worked figures (hypothetical inputs)

The network's emergency supply days in these examples are taken as 5.

| Most recent paid network claim for the drug | Today | Supply on hand | Review bridge |
|---|---|---|---|
| 30 days, dated day 0 | Day 27 | 3 | 5 less 3, that is 2 |
| 30 days, dated day 0 | Day 29 | 1 | 4 |
| 30 days, dated day 0 | Day 40 | 0 (never below zero) | 5 |
| 90 days, dated day 0 | Day 60 | 30 | 0 (never below zero) |
| None | — | 0 | 5 |

## Reading the definition

- The supply on hand is counted as of today, not as of the day the review case was opened.
- The horizon less the supply on hand can never give a negative bridge; it stops at zero.
